RAW warnings above RESOLVED. Both func_ov025_0211123c and func_ov025_021112e0 were carried verbatim inside their own extern "C" blocks, and both blocks then had to be reconciled by hand against the merged include set. func_ov025_0211123c carried a local 30-slot `struct dActor_c` (f00..f29) purely to spell one virtual call; that is a hard redefinition once daDgr_c.h -> dBgActor_c.h -> dActor_c.h brings in the real dActor_c, so it was deleted and the call now goes through daDgr_c::OnAimedAtWithEgg(), the real slot 29. func_ov025_021112e0 needed the Matrix4x3 fix recorded below. Neither is a `CONFLICT:` note, so tools/check_tubuild_conflicts.py's NOTE_RE does not read either one, and no /* TUBUILD CONFLICT */ marker was ever emitted into the source.

TWO MERGE CONFLICTS THAT tubuild's DETECTOR DOES NOT LOOK FOR, both of which would have failed to compile and both reported under `no cross-file conflicts detected`. (1) The two SharedFilePtr handles arrived with contradictory types: `extern int data_ov025_02113a68[]` from the CleanupResources shard and `extern SharedFilePtr data_ov025_02113a68` from the InitResources shard, same for _02113a60. Unified on the object spelling, which lets both call sites be ordinary C++ (`.Release()` and a plain reference argument) with no cast. (2) The local `struct dActor_c` described above. The detector does not compare types and does not compare against real headers, so it saw neither.

THE ONLY BYTE-LEVEL REGRESSION THE MERGE CAUSED, and it is the include-union hazard rather than field-address CSE. func_ov025_021112e0 was the sole DIFF in the first verify of the merged TU -- a function nobody had touched. Matrix4x3 has two guarded 0x30-byte spellings, common.h's flat `s32 m[12]` and math/Matrix.h's `Matrix3x3 r; Vector3 t`, and whichever a TU reaches first stands. As a one-function shard this file included common.h with nothing ahead of it and got the flat one; merged, daDgr_c.h -> dBgW_KcMbg.h -> math/Matrix.h arrives first and common.h's guard stands down, which changed the codegen of the whole-matrix assignment `o->m = *(Matrix4x3*)(self + 0xf0)`. Spelling that one copy against a local flat `struct Mat12 { s32 m[12]; }` restored 9/9 and makes the function immune to any future include reordering.

DESTRUCTOR ORDER: the cartridge puts D1 at 0x021111a0 BELOW D0 at 0x021111e4 and carries no D2 anywhere in ov025. That is the reproducible direction -- exactly what mwccarm 2004/b56 emits from an inline in-class virtual destructor -- so this TU promotes WHOLE and needs no subset licensing. include/daDgr_c.h previously declared `virtual ~daDgr_c();` out of line, reasoning by analogy with include/BigBrickBlock.h's leaf-class convention; the ROM's own addresses refute that analogy and the header is now `virtual ~daDgr_c() {}` declared first. Each of the two shards had also carried its own out-of-line definition, harmless in isolation but a duplicate definition once merged; both are deleted and the header body is the single source of both variants.

compiler_only_output IS 12 ROWS, AND THIS CLASS IS THE MEASUREMENT PASS FOR IT. notes/data/tu-promotion-queue.tsv lists daDgr_c with no sibling_oracle and `compiler-only:unknown(... measure directly ...)`, defaulting the route to text-only. The route IS text-only and the count IS 12, derived: 2 x (4 ancestors + self) = 10 RTTI rows, + 1 _ZTV7daDgr_c + 1 Vector3 = 12. No file-local anonymous struct holds it, so there is no 13th genuinely-homeless row. Every one of the 12 has a configured ROM home in some module's symbols.txt (arm9, ov002 and ov025), so all 12 license as deadstrip-data -- deadstrip-duplicate for the one function -- and externalized_output is EMPTY. Nothing here takes the non-promotable canonical-import route.

VTABLE EXTENT IS PROVEN BY THE FOLLOWING WORD. _ZTV7daDgr_c has 32 slots: the address point is 0x02113760, the last slot is at 0x021137dc, and the next word at 0x021137e0 is 0x44616437 -- little-endian bytes 37 64 61 44, the ASCII "7daD" that begins the next type-name string, not a code pointer. Emitted storage is therefore 0x02113758..0x021137e0 = 0x88 bytes, which is the size tubuild verify reports independently (2 preamble words + 32 slots). Own slots are exactly {0, 3, 6, 9, 16, 17}, MEASURED by word-diffing the table against _ZTV10dBgActor_c (ov002 0x0210ae38): exactly six words differ and every other word is byte-identical, so this class overrides nothing else and adds no new virtual. Slot 31 is 0x020ee55c, dBgActor_c's own Kill, inherited.
